notes: Prefix-matches dir segments against a base-path-to-slug map built from ancestors, which is correct and handles disablePathToLower keys, but it is a somewhat verbose duplicate of a simpler walk and has only a single test.

Builds a prefix-keyed slug map from the page's ancestors and rewrites the dir per path element; this correctly handles nested and non-section intermediate dirs and respects DisablePathToLower, though the Dir field is optional with a fallback rather than replacing the old logic, and it edits the docs folder.

Passes a map from base path to slug into the descriptor and applies it via prefix matching in CreateTargetPaths, which is correct and handles intermediate dirs but is more machinery than needed; there is a single test.
Passes a map of section-path to slug in the descriptor and applies it in CreateTargetPaths, which is correct and readable, but the test never exercises a nested section that has its own slug.

Structurally closest to the reference, but `parentDir + "/" + slug` drops any non-section directory between a slugged section and its parent (e.g. /docs/misc/why), unlike the reference's rel-prefix handling.

Structurally closest to the reference with an always-set Dir, but when a section has a slug it returns parentDir+"/"+slug, dropping any intermediate non-section directories (e.g. /docs/misc/why becomes /docs/<slug>).

Looks up each path segment in the branch tree, pairing normalized and unnormalized dirs, so it handles non-section intermediate dirs and disablePathToLower; the tests cover nested, misc/why, taxonomy, auto-created term and case-preserving cases, though the exact-match check via LongestPrefix is a bit odd.

Correct and very well tested, including sections under non-section dirs and DisablePathToLower, but it does a per-segment tree lookup using LongestPrefix as an exact Get and adds two descriptor fields where one would do.

Uses the same re-parse-the-path trick as C2 but walks the Parent chain instead; the tests are good, including disablePathToLower with a spaced slug, though there is no bounds check and the re-parse is hacky.

Walks the parents and re-parses a slug-substituted path into a new paths.Path for both page and section; compact and thoroughly tested (nested sections, DisablePathToLower, a slug with a space), but re-parsing to rewrite desc.Path is an indirect approach.
Swaps slugs into the unnormalized file path and re-parses it into a new paths.Path, which works without touching the descriptor but is a hacky round trip through the path parser.

Works by querying pageMap tree internals and re-parsing a new paths.Path with slugs substituted, which mutates desc.Path itself; this is clever but hackier and more fragile than computing a dir string.
A concise Parent-chain walk that replaces segments by depth with a bounds check and an optional Dir fallback; one broad test covers spaced slugs, non-section dirs and taxonomy/term.

Compact parent walk that replaces path segments by depth index, correct for nested sections, non-section dirs and unnormalized paths; tests cover a slug containing a space, a non-section dir, and taxonomy/term.

Recursively builds a slugged section base using path.Dir, which keeps intermediate dirs, and rewrites the container dir with a boundary-checked prefix swap; it is clean and minimal, with one broad test.

Recursive section-base computation close to the reference, preserving intermediate non-section dirs and doing a careful boundary-checked prefix swap for container dirs; it adds some descriptor helper machinery but is robust.

Builds a depth-keyed slug map from Ancestors and works, but allocates a map for every page and returns a dir without a leading slash, which is inconsistent with the other paths; there is a single test.
Simple depth-indexed slug map over the page and its ancestors applied to the dir elements; clean, correct and well tested, including the English side remaining unchanged.

Replaces segments by ancestor depth with a fallback to the old dirs, and the tests cover uglyURLs and file-less terms; the Reverse() call is unnecessary, and appending to its possibly cached result is slightly fragile.

Correct depth-indexed replacement with good tests (uglyURLs, term without content file), but it calls Ancestors().Reverse() for no reason, hitting the sort cache and appending onto a potentially shared cached slice.
